value.scope:
Kalton's question asks whether uniform discreteness of a metric space forces its Lipschitz-free space to have the bounded approximation property. The formalization constructs a countable metric space with all distinct points at distance at least one whose real Lipschitz-free space has the approximation property but fails every bounded approximation bound. The metric space is unbounded and not proper.

The earlier quantitative renorming result for real $\ell_1$ is retained: for each integer $p\ge1$, an equivalent complete norm has the $2B_p$-bounded approximation property but fails the $p$-bounded approximation property, where $B_p=300p^2+150p+5$.

statements.name: thm:main
statements.text:
\label{thm:main}
There is a countable, unbounded, nonproper pointed metric space $(M,d,o)$
such that $d(x,y)\ge1$ for distinct points and $\F(M)$ has AP but fails
$\lambda$-BAP for every finite $\lambda\ge1$.

statements.name: thm:blocks
statements.text:
\label{thm:blocks}
For each integer $p\ge1$, there are a bounded countably infinite pointed
metric space $(M_p,d_p,o)$ and a finite set $A_p\subseteq M_p$ containing
$o$ such that
\[
 d_p(x,y)\ge1\quad(x\ne y),\qquad
 \operatorname{diam}M_p\le B_p:=300p^2+150p+5,
\]
and every bounded finite-rank linear operator
$T_0:\F(M_p)\to\F(M_p)$ with $\norm{T_0}\le p$ satisfies
\[
 \max_{a\in A_p}\norm{T_0\delta_a-\delta_a}\ge\frac12.
\]
